toc.title: What it deliberately does not read

preamble:
Holding the compiler's reads of a node's label or namespace, and of a backend's name, to display, a copied label or a marked site, never a decision (gh-ocannl-1783).

The reading behind test/operations/label_dispatch_scan (gh-ocannl-1783): the compiler under arrayjit/lib/ reads a tensor node's label, namespace or names spelled from them, and a backend's name, only to show them, to copy a label onto a node it mints, or at a site that says why the read decides nothing.

A node's label and namespace are public inputs to Tnode.create: a user's { fragment } tensor has the label head a masked MMA fragment had, and a user tensor can carry any namespace. So a compiler decision keyed on them can be forged by a tensor name. The defect recurred as Online_softmax.fold_tile_role (tile roles by namespace and label, gh-ocannl-1722), Schedule.is_fragment (a "fragment" label head, gh-ocannl-1721) and backend-kind tests by substrings of the backend name (gh-ocannl-1723), and earlier as gh-ocannl-793. Each fix replaced the spelling with a membership the compiler fills, keyed by the node's uid, or with the Backend_intf capability facts a backend states.

The walker is Debug_name_scan's, read fail-closed: a reference is refused unless it sits in an accepted position, so a decision form nobody listed is refused rather than missed. This module states the rule's references and its extra accepted positions; the walker's own forms (the printed, claim-label, needle, transparent and alias positions, the trust in sink names) are in that module's header.
content:
What it reads

Every .ml under arrayjit/lib/, parsed by ppxlib, a [%string]'s interpolations included.

  • References: an application of debug_name or label_name (under any module path; a bare one a parameter or a pattern binds is the parameter's value, not the function); label and namespace spelled qualified (Tn.label, Tnode.namespace), or bare where no binding of the source is in scope (an open brought them in) -- a bare local label is a common name and is not read; a read of a record field named label or namespace under any type path (tn.Tn.label, r.label) -- fields of other records are read too, the loud direction; and any identifier named backend_name (Context.backend_name ctx, Backends.backend_name b, a parameter or a pattern variable named so), read unapplied as the value itself.
  • Accepted: the Debug_name_scan positions (printed or raised, a claim label, a ~substring needle, an alias's body), and:
  1. composed into a message: an operand of ^ or sprintf, or a [%string] interpolation: the text it is composed into is a message, and the spelling no longer stands alone in it. String.concat stays transparent, since a label list joined whole is the label;
  2. a log payload: anywhere inside a [%log...] extension (ppx_minidebug), which is evaluated only to be shown;
  3. raised: the payload of a User_error constructor (under any path);
  4. copied onto a new node: the ~label or ~namespace argument of Tn.create / Tnode.create, a list cons there transparent (~label:("tile" :: like.Tn.label));
  5. forwarded: a ~backend_name labelled argument of any call, whose callee binds the parameter under the same name and is judged there;
  6. marked: the reference carries [\@message_only "<reason>"] (a message by a road the walker does not follow, such as a local formatter) or [\@label_read "<reason>"] (a read that decides nothing a forged name could steer: Tnode's own identity, the user's choice of a backend by name, an identity key compared for equality), each with a reason of at least two words.
  • Refused: every other reference -- in a match or an if, an argument of String.equal, String.is_prefix, = or any other function, bound by a let, put in a tuple or a record; a reference field destructured in a pattern; a ~backend_name parameter bound to another name.

What it deliberately does not read

  • A decision on composed text (String.equal ("x" ^ Tn.label tn) "xfragment"): composition is read as display, and a dispatch spelled that way is beyond what this scan guards against.
  • Flow past the positions: a string a let binds from an accepted position, and a message built and then compared, are not followed. The rule is that a label reaches display, a copied label or a marked site, not a data-flow proof.
  • A bare label or namespace a let of the source binds, including Tnode's own top-level label: inside tnode.ml the node's fields are read as fields, which this scan reads.
  • Backend names under other spellings: a backend module's name, Device.name, a string a let binds from Context.backend_name under another name (the let itself is refused), a callee that renames a ~backend_name parameter is refused at the callee.
  • Tnode.get_debug_name and the code_name field (the renderer's minted name).
val rule : Debug_name_scan.rule
val positions : Base.string Base__List.t
val scan : file:string -> string -> Debug_name_scan.report
